long_biography.plain_text:
Three bond offerings for Malaysia's development fund brought former Goldman Sachs banker Tim Leissner into the centre of the 1MDB case. He helped arrange the fundraising and admitted participating in a scheme to pay bribes and launder its proceeds. His guilty plea was followed by cooperation with U.S. investigators, including testimony against a former colleague.

U.S. regulators permanently barred him from the securities industry. A federal court sentenced him to two years in prison in 2025, and he began serving the sentence in 2026. His cooperation was considered at sentencing, alongside the harm caused by the scheme.
